findings.issue: Full-ring flop vs 9 ranges (scenario 7) has only ~12% headroom against its 80 ms reference-machine target, so the SPEC-12 command is close to flaky on a slightly busier or slower machine.
findings.evidence: Three runs of `EQUITY_PERF_SCALE=1 npx vitest run tests/advice/equity.perf.test.ts` on Node 22.18.0: p95 70.20, 70.97, 70.53 ms (target 80). The other scenarios have >= 2x headroom. At ~2.8% whole-deal acceptance for 9 random combos on a flop (~35 rejections per accepted trial), most of the time goes to the rejection loop and per-trial work, not the 300k evaluations (~20 ms).
findings.fix: No change needed to pass. If the judge's SPEC-12 run is marginal, cut per-trial cost in the sampler loop (e.g. avoid allocating the [a, b] tuple in table.setHole per opponent per trial by writing hands[p+1][0..1] directly, and avoid the `?? 0` reads in the hot loop) rather than changing the spec's trial count or rejection rule.

findings.issue: `expect(191_646).toBeLessThanOrEqual(EXACT_EVALUATION_LIMIT)` asserts on a literal; it adds nothing beyond the estimate and method assertions just above it.
findings.evidence: The preceding lines already assert the estimate is 191,646 and the method is 'exact', which fails if the limit drops below 191,646.
findings.fix: Drop the line, or assert `EXACT_EVALUATION_LIMIT` toBe(200_000) if pinning the constant is the intent.

summary: All SPEC items implemented and tested. Sampler is statistically sound: per-opponent uniform combo pick with whole-deal rejection gives a uniform distribution over valid deals, and runout drawing by rejection from 52 is uniform over subsets; a scratch comparison against exactEquity on overlapping 60-combo ranges (3-way turn) converged from ~0.4 pp at 30k to <=0.13 pp at 300k trials, and a tie-heavy case matched win/tie/equity. Tie shares use integer 2520 units (exact for any split up to 10). estimateEvaluations matches the rule-3 formula and all SPEC-08 examples including the 191,646/201,600 boundary (A-12 river example accepted). Canonicalisation (sorted hero/board/combos, dead/duplicate combo removal, stable opponent sort) and mapping back via order[i] are correct; the SPEC-09 property test uses distinct ranges and would catch an identity or inverted mapping (covers the gap noted in A-13). Generator is independent of src/advice (only evaluate/parseCards via runnerImport) and is cross-checked against the equity module on a flop case. SPEC-14 greps print nothing. Full-ring perf measured at ~70-71 ms p95 vs 80 ms target: passes, thin margin (MINOR). No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings.
